observed_problem: All five within-swing native contact releases in V35 coincide with a lower composed knee goal at the next command. The slew-limited reference actually decreases in three, including the first front-left release. The other two references are still rising toward a lagging goal, so a lower goal is not the same as an applied downward reference. The existing formula switches off amplitude*0.40 knee assistance immediately when support disappears. Exact same-input algebra isolates this branch sensitivity; adjacent physical rows also change phase, amplitude and pose. This is a testable command discontinuity, not proof that it causes every short cycle.
selected_change: For the new policy only, replace the raw contact-conditioned swing knee target with amplitude*(0.82*1.75+0.40)*sin(pi*phase/72) for 0<=phase<72; use exactly zero at phase 72 and throughout stance. Keep the existing support-knee composition, joint bounds and reference slew. This is continuous in value at the swing endpoints, not a claim of derivative continuity or a new physical clearance guarantee. No contact-history latch or new fitted coefficient is introduced.
coefficient_provenance: The 0.82 knee-flexion coefficient, 1.75 scale, 0.40 existing contact assistance, 72-step swing and 1.1-rad knee maximum are the observed native constants/bounds. Peak lift is unchanged from the old loaded swing peak. The existing amplitude cap 1.1/(0.82*1.75+0.40)=0.5994550408719347 is preserved, not increased or fitted to V35's outcome.
